name_en: Nielsen fixed-point theorem (exact theorem identity open)
statement_blocker: The catalog gloss names a theory, not a proposition. It does not choose among fixed-point-class construction, index and essentiality, Nielsen-number finiteness or homotopy invariance, the Nielsen lower bound, or a surface/minimum theorem; nor does it fix the class of spaces, map and homotopy category, index convention, quantifier order, hypotheses, conclusion, or boundary cases. Selecting one would invent or substitute mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted source must fix the class of spaces (for example a closed surface, compact connected polyhedron, ANR/ENR, or manifold), dimension and boundary conditions, continuous self-map and homotopy category, fixed-point-class representation, index theory, cardinality representation, universe levels, and required topological structures.
conclusion: Open: the catalog does not say whether the target constructs fixed-point classes, proves finiteness or index properties, establishes homotopy invariance or a lower bound, realizes the minimum, or conjoins several source results.
degenerate_case_status: no case is excluded before an exact source proposition is selected; every listed candidate case remains pending source and scope review
candidate_scope_not_credited: partition fixed points into Nielsen classes via paths and a homotopy of the self-map
define the same classes through lifts or Reidemeister classes and prove correspondence
attach an index to each class and define essential classes and the Nielsen number
prove homotopy invariance of the Nielsen number
prove that every map homotopic to f has at least N(f) fixed points under source-fixed hypotheses
prove a surface or higher-dimensional realization theorem identifying N(f) with a homotopy-class minimum
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty, singleton, disconnected, noncompact, boundary-bearing, or non-triangulable spaces
maps with no fixed points, infinitely many fixed points, or infinitely many fixed-point classes
identity and constant maps and maps homotopic to fixed-point-free representatives
inessential zero-index classes and index normalization at boundary fixed points
free, relative, or based homotopy and path versus lift/Reidemeister class definitions
natural, finite-cardinal, or cardinal-valued counts and comparisons
dimension, compactness, connectedness, local contractibility, ANR/ENR, and finiteness hypotheses
excluded_substitutions: a generic fixed-point set, homotopy, fundamental-group, or covering-space interface presented as a Nielsen theorem
a structure or hypothesis that assumes the requested invariant, lower bound, or minimum conclusion
a convenient finite or interval theorem substituted for a source theorem about surfaces or polyhedra
the catalog title, date, attribution, or untrusted verified label used as proof evidence
